_comment: Scope-detection config for the Data Quality Gate (distinct from data-standards' .data-standards.json). Read by .claude/skills/data-quality-gate/scripts/scope_detect.py, stdlib-only, no PyYAML/psycopg needed for this step so an irrelevant PR returns NOT_APPLICABLE cheaply and fast.
_migration_command_note: dashboard/database/migrations/ is NOT self-sufficient — it's a set of incremental deltas layered on top of the base schema in infrastructure/supabase/00_complete-schema.sql (confirmed live: applying migrations/ alone to an empty throwaway Postgres fails immediately with 'relation "conversations" does not exist', since that table — and most of the core schema — is only defined in 00_complete-schema.sql, never inside migrations/ itself). 01_rls-policies.sql is deliberately SKIPPED — confirmed it references Supabase's own built-in "auth" schema (auth.uid()/auth.jwt()), which only exists inside a real hosted Supabase project and fails on any plain throwaway Postgres; it also contains zero schema-structural statements (no CREATE TABLE/ADD COLUMN/CREATE INDEX, purely 124 row-level-security policies), so skipping it has no effect on what this gate actually checks. 11 real migration files (plus the base schema) also GRANT to Supabase's managed 'authenticated'/'service_role' roles, which don't exist on a plain Postgres either — confirmed live ('role "service_role" does not exist'); migration_command creates both as empty, no-login stand-in roles first (matching how Supabase's own local-dev CLI already handles this), safe unconditionally since every CI run gets a brand-new, role-free container. dashboard/database/migrations/009_create_ama_tables.sql also fails live ('schema "auth" does not exist') — unlike 01_rls-policies.sql this file cannot be skipped, since it mixes real CREATE TABLE statements (ama_conversations, ama_messages, ama_query_audit) together with 4 auth.uid() references inside its own RLS policies (confirmed via grep — no other migration file or the base schema references the auth schema at all). Fixed by creating a stand-in auth schema with a stub uid() function that always returns NULL::uuid before applying anything — this lets the RLS policy statements succeed harmlessly (they just never match a real user in this throwaway container) while preserving all the real table-creation DDL in 009, matching the same reasoning already used for the authenticated/service_role stand-ins above. OPEN FINDING, not a CI-environment gap — flagged for the schema/BYOF owner, not resolved here: infrastructure/supabase/00_complete-schema.sql:1043 declares byof_plans.summary_embedding as a dimensionless 'vector' column, but dashboard/database/migrations/017_create_byof_tables.sql:37 declares the same column as VECTOR(1536) and (line 70-71) builds an hnsw index on it — pgvector rejects hnsw/ivfflat indexes on dimensionless vector columns. No later migration file ever adds a dimension to the base schema's column. On a fresh apply (exactly what this gate does), 017's CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is a no-op against the table 00_complete-schema.sql already created, so the column never gets VECTOR(1536) and the index build fails ('column does not have dimensions', confirmed live). Whether the REAL production database's column currently has a dimension could not be checked from static files alone. For the dry-run only, migration_command strips just the CREATE INDEX ... USING hnsw statement out of 017_create_byof_tables.sql via sed before applying it (everything else in 017 — the 4 CREATE TABLEs, its other indexes, its trigger — applies unmodified); this is a workaround for testing, not a fix, and the real inconsistency should be checked against production before being resolved for real. dashboard/database/migrations/019_rls_related_tables.sql also fails live ('role "portal_app_user" does not exist') — same category as authenticated/service_role, an app-managed role only ever referenced in GRANT statements (019, 020_invitations_and_scope_updates.sql, 020_invitations_and_scope_updates_fixed.sql); fixed the same way, with an empty no-login stand-in role. Separately, HYGIENE FINDING: 020_invitations_and_scope_updates.sql and 020_invitations_and_scope_updates_fixed.sql are duplicate-numbered — confirmed via diff that _fixed is the same migration made idempotent (its own comment says 'FIXED - Idempotent', it adds a DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS guard the original lacks, and drops leftover commented-out verification queries), i.e. the original was superseded in place rather than given its own next number. Applying both back-to-back risks double-applying the same CREATE TABLE/POLICY statements. The original (020_invitations_and_scope_updates.sql, without _fixed) is excluded from both scope.json's exclude list and migration_command's apply loop — only the _fixed version is applied. dashboard/database/migrations/add_lesson_plan_pdf_url.sql (an unnumbered file) also fails live ('column "pdf_url" already exists') — confirmed 00_complete-schema.sql already has lesson_plans.pdf_url (line 415) and its accompanying index (line 3338, already IF NOT EXISTS-guarded); this migration's change was folded into the base schema snapshot at some point and is now redundant/superseded, same category as the duplicate 020 file. Excluded from both scope.json's exclude list and migration_command's apply loop. (Checked the other unnumbered file, add_portal_authentication.sql, for the same issue — it already uses ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS throughout, so it's safe to apply as-is and needed no change.)
migration_command: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c 'CREATE ROLE authenticated; CREATE ROLE service_role; CREATE ROLE portal_app_user;' || exit 1; psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c 'CREATE SCHEMA auth; CREATE FUNCTION auth.uid() RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$ SELECT NULL::uuid $$;' || exit 1; psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f infrastructure/supabase/00_complete-schema.sql || exit 1; for f in dashboard/database/migrations/*.sql; do bn="$(basename "$f")"; if [ "$bn" = '020_invitations_and_scope_updates.sql' ] || [ "$bn" = 'add_lesson_plan_pdf_url.sql' ]; then continue; elif [ "$bn" = '017_create_byof_tables.sql' ]; then sed '/CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_byof_plans_embedding/,/USING hnsw (summary_embedding vector_cosine_ops);/d' "$f" | psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 || exit 1; else psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "$f" || exit 1; fi; done
